title: Practice Paper 01 · Sourabh sir
subtitle: AIML ZG565 comprehensive (EC-3) practice · open book · 40 marks · 7 questions · fully solved

lesson.title: Try it on your own: how to use this paper
lesson.lead: Sit it like the real exam first. Only then open the solutions.

items: Set a timer for **2 hours** (the paper says 2½, but your real exam on 6 Dec is 2 hours, so practise at that speed).
Open book: keep only your textbook and notes, as in the exam.
Write every answer on paper, showing each step and stating assumptions in one line.
Use natural logs unless told otherwise; round to 4 decimals.
When the time is up, open **Worked problems** and mark yourself, question by question.

blocks.label: Why this paper matters
blocks.text: Five of its seven questions are your top-five chapters (30 of 40 marks). It also has the 4-mark **model evaluation** question that the past papers never asked, so do not skip CS 15.

blocks.label: Marking yourself
blocks.text: Give yourself the marks shown in each question's brackets. A score of 30+ here means you are on track.

worked.title: Q1 · Closed-form least squares and ridge (6 marks)

problem.text: Machine age x (years) and maintenance cost y (₹ thousand): (2, 8), (3, 8), (5, 14), (7, 22), (8, 21).

(a) Closed-form θ₀ and θ₁ for y = θ₀ + θ₁x. [2.5 M] (b) Predict y at x = 4. [0.5 M] (c) SSE, SST and R². [1.5 M] (d) Ridge on centred data, minimise Σ((yᵢ − ȳ) − θ₁(xᵢ − x̄))² + λθ₁²: the ridge slope for λ = 2, and the λ that exactly halves the least-squares slope. [1.5 M]

steps.label: Where marks are lost
steps.text: Using Σxy/Σx² (line through the origin); writing SST as Σ(ŷ − ȳ)²; thinking ridge can make the slope exactly 0.

worked.title: Q2 · kNN regression and locally weighted regression (6 marks)

problem.text: (a) 3-NN mean. [1 M] (b) Distance-weighted 3-NN, wᵢ = 1/dᵢ. [1.5 M] (c) LWR ŷ = θ₀ + θ₁x on the 3 neighbours, Gaussian kernel Kᵢ = exp(−(xᵢ − x_q)²/(2τ²)) with τ = 3, update θⱼ ← θⱼ + αΣKᵢ(yᵢ − ŷᵢ)xᵢⱼ (xᵢ₀ = 1), start θ₀ = θ₁ = 1, α = 0.02: one update, and the prediction at x_q before and after. [3.5 M]

steps.label: Where marks are lost
steps.text: Choosing neighbours by y instead of x; not dividing by Σw; using 2τ instead of 2τ².

worked.title: Q3 · Polynomial and RBF kernels (6 marks)

problem.text: (a) 3 × 3 polynomial Gram matrix. [2 M] (b) Explicit φ(x), φ(u), φ(v), and check φ(u)ᵀφ(v) = K(u, v). [2 M] (c) ‖φ(u) − φ(v)‖² without φ. [1 M] (d) RBF value for each pair; most similar pair. [1 M]

steps.label: Where marks are lost
steps.text: Dropping the +2; missing the √2 and 2 factors in φ; not squaring the distance in RBF.

problem.text: (a) L(a), dropping constants. [1.5 M] (b) General MLE in terms of n₀ zeros out of n rolls. [2 M] (c) â for this data. [1.5 M] (d) Using â, P(roll = 2) and the expected number of 2s in 40 rolls. [1 M]

steps.label: (b)
steps.text: ℓ = n₀ ln a + (n − n₀) ln(1 − a); ℓ′ = n₀/a − (n − n₀)/(1 − a) = 0 ⇒ **â = n₀/n**

steps.label: Where marks are lost
steps.text: Differentiating L instead of ln L; forgetting to plug â back in for part (d).

problem.text: Jobs (Traffic, Distance km, y): J1 (High, 8, 48), J2 (High, 2, 36), J3 (High, 6, 42), J4 (Low, 4, 34), J5 (Low, 9, 51), J6 (Low, 2, 26). F₀ = mean(y), rᵢ = yᵢ − F(xᵢ), leaves = mean residual, η = 0.1. Tree 1: Low → L_A; else Distance ≤ 6 → L_B; else L_C.

(a) F₀ and residuals. [1 M] (b) L_A, L_B, L_C. [1.5 M] (c) F₁ for every job and training MSE before and after tree 1. [2 M] (d) Tree 2 splits Distance ≤ 5.5 on the new residuals: its two leaf values and F₂(J3). [1.5 M]

steps.label: Where marks are lost
steps.text: Adding the full leaf value instead of η × leaf; fitting tree 2 to the old residuals.

worked.title: Q6 · K-means and initial centroids (6 marks)

problem.text: 1-D data: 0, 9, 11, 12, 19, 26, 28. K = 2. Analyst A starts at (10, 19), analyst B at (0, 15).
(a) Run from A's start to convergence. [2 M] (b) Run from B's start. [2 M] (c) SSE of both; which is better? [1.5 M] (d) One initialisation scheme that reduces this risk. [0.5 M]

steps.label: (d)
steps.text: **K-means++** seeding, or several random restarts keeping the lowest SSE

steps.label: Where marks are lost
steps.text: Assuming both starts give the same answer; comparing by iterations instead of SSE.

problem.text: 200 actual fraud, 3600 negatives. M1: TP 130, FP 160, FN 70, TN 3440. M2: TP 120, FP 100, FN 80, TN 3500.
(a) Accuracy, precision, recall and F1 for both. [2.5 M] (b) Higher F1? [0.5 M] (c) Rule: recall ≥ 0.61. Which model meets it, and how many fraud cases does it miss? [1 M]

steps.label: (c)
steps.text: Only **M1** has recall ≥ 0.61; it misses **70** fraud cases (FN)

steps.label: Where marks are lost
steps.text: Swapping FP and FN in recall; judging by accuracy on imbalanced data; averaging P and R arithmetically.
